chapter_meta.chapter_title: An Introduction to the Closed Catalan
chapter_meta.description: Explores the fundamental move order, positional concepts, and structural mechanisms of the Closed Catalan, highlighting White's king safety, the long-range pressure of the g2-bishop, and the strategic preparation of central breaks.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Control key central squares and maintain opening flexibility.
core_trunk.explanation: White develops the king's knight to control d4 and e5 while avoiding premature central commitments.
core_trunk.hint: Develop your king's knight toward the center.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Stake an immediate classical claim in the center.
core_trunk.explanation: Black occupies the center with the d-pawn, controlling e4 and c4.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Establish a firm classical foothold in the center.
core_trunk.explanation: White supports the c4 square and stakes out space on e5 and c5.
core_trunk.hint: Advance your queen's pawn to claim central space.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Develop a kingside minor piece and contest the e4 square.
core_trunk.explanation: Black reinforces the d5 pawn and prepares kingside development.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Challenge Black's central pawn anchor on d5.
core_trunk.explanation: White attacks Black's d5 point to create central tension and open lines for queenside development.
core_trunk.hint: Strike at Black's central pawn with your c-pawn.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Solidify the center and prepare kingside bishop development.
core_trunk.explanation: Black protects d5 solidly while opening the diagonal for the dark-squared bishop.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Prepare the signature Catalan kingside fianchetto.
core_trunk.explanation: White readies the g2-square for the light-squared bishop to dominate the long diagonal h1-a8.
core_trunk.hint: Prepare to fianchetto your king's bishop.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Complete harmonious kingside minor piece development.
core_trunk.explanation: Black develops the bishop modestly to e7, prioritizing rapid castling and maintaining a solid structure.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Deploy the Catalan bishop onto its optimal outpost.
core_trunk.explanation: The bishop takes up its post on g2, exerting long-term latent pressure against Black's queenside.
core_trunk.hint: Place your bishop on the long diagonal.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Tuck the king away into safety.
core_trunk.explanation: Black completes kingside castling before resolving central tension.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Secure the white king behind a solid pawn fortress.
core_trunk.explanation: White castles kingside, bringing the king to safety and mobilizing the h1-rook.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Construct a solid central pawn wedge.
core_trunk.explanation: Black establishes the Closed Catalan pawn triangle (c6-d5-e6) to bludgeon the scope of the g2-bishop.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Overprotect c4 and prepare central expansion.
core_trunk.explanation: White positions the queen to control the c-file, defend c4, and prepare the thematic e2-e4 thrust.
core_trunk.hint: Centralize your queen on c2 to guard c4 and control e4.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Develop the queen's knight to support central breaks.
core_trunk.explanation: Black reinforces the d5-point and prepares eventual freeing thrusts like ...c5 or ...e5.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Place a rook opposite Black's central axis.
core_trunk.explanation: White positions the rook on the semi-open d-file, supporting central operations and deterring freeing pawn pushes.
core_trunk.hint: Position your rook on the d-file opposite Black's queen.

core_trunk.strategic_idea: Prepare queenside fianchetto to activate the problem bishop.
core_trunk.explanation: Black prepares to place the light-squared bishop on b7 or a6 to contest White's positional grip.

trigger_move.strategic_idea: Accelerate development of the queenside bishop without committing the knight.
trigger_move.explanation: Black prepares to activate the c8-bishop directly via b7 or a6 while keeping options open for the queen's knight.

continuation.strategic_idea: Maintain positional pressure down the d-file.
continuation.explanation: White develops the rook to d1, maintaining flexibility and discouraging an immediate central counter-break.
continuation.hint: Develop your rook to the d-file to reinforce the center.

continuation.strategic_idea: Complete the fianchetto of the light-squared bishop.
continuation.explanation: Black places the bishop on the long diagonal to counter White's Catalan pressure.

trigger_move.strategic_idea: Employ a flexible waiting move and support the e-file.
trigger_move.explanation: Black delays the queenside commitment, preparing to route the knight via f8 to g6 while bolstering the e6-point.

continuation.strategic_idea: Reinforce c4 and prepare dark-squared bishop development.
continuation.explanation: White secures the queenside pawn chain and prepares to develop the bishop to b2 or a3.
continuation.hint: Solidify your c4-pawn and prepare to develop your queen's bishop.

continuation.explanation: Black proceeds with developing the light-squared bishop to b7 now that the kingside position is consolidated.

summary_takeaways: The Catalan bishop on g2 exerts persistent pressure down the h1-a8 diagonal against Black's queenside.
The c6-d5-e6 pawn triangle establishes a solid barrier for Black but restricts the light-squared bishop on c8.
White's queen on c2 performs multiple duties: protecting c4, observing the c-file, and preparing e2-e4.
Central rook  on d1 serves both prophylactic and active roles, restraining Black's liberating pawn breaks.
